seo.title: Why Binary Search Finds Anything In 20 Guesses
seo.hook: A million names, and twenty guesses is enough. Every guess throws away half of what is lef
seo.description: You can halve a sorted search space without ever writing an off-by-one bug.

scenes.narration: A million names, and twenty guesses is enough. Every guess throws away half of what is left.

scenes.headline: Guess the [middle]
scenes.caption: position four holds sixteen
scenes.narration: |While left is less than or equal to right, keep guessing. That equals sign matters, because it lets the search look at a single remaining item. |Mid equals left plus right, integer-divided by two. Zero plus nine is nine, and nine halved rounding down is %four, because those two slashes mean divide and throw away the remainder. So >we look at position four, which holds ^sixteen. |Is sixteen our target? No, twenty-three is bigger. And because the list is sorted, everything left of sixteen is smaller still, so none of it can possibly be twenty-three.

lines.detail: Keep guessing while the range still holds something.
The middle of what is left. // rounds down.
Is the middle our target? Not this time.

scenes.premise: A sorted row of numbers, and one target to find. It is higher-or-lower: every guess throws away half of whatever is still left.

scenes.headline: Guess again, [go left]
scenes.caption: fifty-six is too big
scenes.narration: |New middle: five plus nine is fourteen, halved and rounded down is %seven. >Position seven holds ^fifty-six, which is bigger than twenty-three. Same reasoning as before, mirrored: everything right of fifty-six is bigger than fifty-six, and fifty-six was already too big, so ^all of that can go too. |The else branch fires, right becomes mid minus one, and >the top edge drops to %six. Two guesses in, and eight of the ten are already out of the running.

lines.detail: The middle of what is left: position seven.
Too big, so pull the top edge down to mid - 1.

scenes.premise: A sorted row of numbers, and one target to find. It is higher-or-lower: every guess throws away half of whatever is still left.

scenes.headline: Found, in [three guesses]
scenes.caption: position five
scenes.narration: |Mid is five plus six halved, rounding down to %five. >Position five holds ^twenty-three. |That's our number, so we return the index, and %the answer's five. Three guesses for ten items. For a phone book with a million names that's about twenty, and for every page Google has indexed, somewhere around thirty-three. Doubling the data costs you one more guess. Every time, forever.

lines.detail: The middle of the last two: position five.
Found it. Hand back the position.
